Qualification note: Harrow & Finch Grocers (harrow-and-finch.example)

Part 1. Can this company be a buyer?

Buyer or vendor: BUYER
Where its revenue comes from: shoppers buy groceries in supermarkets the company runs under its own name.
Store count and country: the store locator lists 62 stores, all in Canada (https://harrow-and-finch.example/stores). Head office is in the same province.
In scope: yes. The sourcing record gives 4,300 employees, which fits a chain of this size. The record carried no scope warnings.

Part 2. Is there a need?

Need: STRONG.
Every store page promotes produce, an in-store bakery and a butcher counter. The sustainability page sets a target to halve food waste by 2032 and reports last year's figure per store (https://harrow-and-finch.example/sustainability/food-waste). Two local news items from the last year mention empty fresh shelves after a long weekend; I treat those as anecdote, not as evidence.

Part 3. How do they order today?

Current approach: BASIC TOOLS (inferred).
An open posting for an Inventory Coordinator describes "maintaining minimum and maximum stock levels per store" and "reviewing suggested orders from the merchandising system" (https://harrow-and-finch.example/careers/inventory-coordinator). No page names a forecasting product, and I found no vendor case study that names the company. This is an inference from one posting.

Part 4. Is there a reason to talk now?

Timing: ACTIVE TRIGGER.
In March the company announced a second distribution centre that will supply fresh departments in 24 stores from the autumn (https://harrow-and-finch.example/news/second-distribution-centre). Moving stores to a new supply point is a natural moment to revisit how orders are set.

Verdict

QUALIFIED, TIER A.

Confidence in this answer: HIGH. The store count, the waste target and the new distribution centre all come from the company's own pages. Only the ordering method is inferred.

Reason for the verdict: a 62-store chain in scope on size and country, with a fresh offer at the centre of its stores and a published target to halve food waste. It is opening a second distribution centre this year, which changes how every store is supplied.

Strongest signal: the company's own news page announces a second distribution centre that will supply fresh departments in 24 stores from the autumn.

Main uncertainty: how store orders are calculated today. The careers page points to fixed stock levels, but no page says so directly.

Roles to contact: supply chain; fresh merchandising; store operations. The leadership page names a Vice President of Supply Chain, but gives no date, so I did not name the person here.

Budget used: 4 web searches, 3 remote page reads, 7 local reads.
